title: incremental-version-fallback-orchestrator-for-private-deployments
creator: Ariana Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an incremental version fallback orchestrator that enables safe, automated control-plane promotions for Private (VPC) deployments. This ticket delivers an orchestration layer and Terraform gating that: (1) progressively promotes a new control-plane version to a subset of tenants; (2) continuously evaluates a multi-signal health score; and (3) automatically triggers a deterministic fallback (rollback) to the previous stable version if health drops below threshold or compatibility invariants fail.

Background: Current private upgrade workflows are manual and rely on ad-hoc canary slices with limited automated rollback triggers. We need a predictable, auditable automation approach that integrates with Terraform modules used by customers' IaC and our private controlplane operator. The orchestrator must be tenant-aware, idempotent, and support fast recovery windows for high-risk changes (e.g., schema migrations, API surface changes).

Scope: Core deliverables for this ticket:
- Orchestrator service (stateless controller) that drives staged Terraform promotions and rollback commands.
- Terraform adapter modules / wrappers to perform plan/apply with a dry-run preflight and drift-aware gating.
- Health scoring pipeline (synthetic probes, telemetry regression checks, API contract checks) that outputs a single monotonic health score for each promotion wave.
- Deterministic fallback policy engine with configurable cool-downs, quarantine windows, and optional manual approval hold.
- Audit trail (work items + events) persisted to customer audit logs and internal runbook entries.

Non-goals: Full UI integration in Console (this ticket is API and operator changes only), and per-tenant UI controls. Those will be follow-ups once the orchestration primitives are stable.
tasks: Design API and state model for orchestrator (waves, wave-ids, wave-scopes, version-contracts)
Spike: Terraform adapter prototype that can run plan -> apply -> dry-run -> revert programmatically (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/private-controlplane)
Implement health scoring microservice (synthetic probes + telemetry rule engine)
Integrate OPA policy check into preflight gating for schema and CRD compatibility
Create Terraform modules/wrappers for tenant-scoped promotion with idempotency tokens
Add audit events to controlplane operator and orchestrator (persist to s3/audit store)
Create runbook and rollback playbook with explicit commands and PR links
Add e2e tests in staging that simulate version badness and confirm automated fallback
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can promote version X -> X+1 for a specified tenant subset using terraform wrappers and record the action in audit logs
Health scoring returns a single score every 30s and triggers automatic fallback if score < 0.65 for 3 consecutive windows
Compatibility preflight (CRD/schema checks) blocks promotion when breaking changes are detected and surfaces a clear error to the runbook
Automated fallback executes deterministic terraform apply to previous version and confirms reconciliation within SLA (target: 5m median for simple controlplane changes)
Integration tests validate both successful promotions and failure scenarios (synthetic failure and slow KV cache behavior) in staging
Telemetry: promotion/fallback events appear in Console-level audit dashboard and correlate with runtime metrics
risks: Terraform non-determinism (drift) causing failed rollbacks — mitigated by plan diff check and idempotency tokens
Operator incompatibility between versions that prevents clean rollback (CRD drift) — mitigated by preflight schema adapter and OPA gating
False positives from health probes causing unnecessary rollbacks — mitigated by multi-signal scoring and consecutive-window policy
Large tenant fleets where rollback requires staggered resource rebinds — will require follow-up for tenant-ordered orchestration
